summary: The cause of the drop is verified: Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor race on Nov 3-4 on a promise of a ban on all new data-center approvals until the Legislature acts, and she takes office Jan 19; this raises the odds of the Texas pause risk the research already carries (weights 0.45 Texas / 0.10 PJM-state), so I rate it minor, not a new fact outside the scenarios. No Vistra release, no PJM or ERCOT action and no thesis trigger (guidance, PJM cap after 2029/30, a lasting Texas block) turned up for Nov 4-5; the Q3 report on Nov 6 before the open is the real test, and the stock (112.89 at the Nov 5 print, below the 115 thesis-break level) is a price move, which is never a trigger on its own.

items.headline: Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor's race; she has pledged a moratorium (a ban) on all data-center approvals until the Legislature passes protections, takes office Jan 19, 2027; Abbott's grid and environmental-permit pauses stay in place during an audit expected to end in December, with no end date given
items.why: Opened the Texas Tribune piece; GV Wire (Nov 4) and Yahoo Finance headlines on the same result were seen in search but not opened. This is the event behind the Nov 4 drop. The research already books a governor-ordered Texas pause (weight 0.45; the thesis-break note names a pause lasting past ERCOT's Dec 10 reports as the failure case), and the 2026-11-05 run's own weight table shows moving from 0.45/0.10 to 0.60/0.20 costs only about 0.2% of the research target (12m), so the election result, which lifts the odds toward the top of that range, is worth roughly -0.2% to -0.5% on those sensitivities (my estimate, not re-run). Not sized: a pause that outlasts the 12-month horizon, the Legislature meeting in January 2027, ending data-center tax breaks and a stricter who-pays-for-the-grid rule, which would sit in the horizon multiple and which the Tribune article does not detail; the Tribune also says the new governor needs the Legislature for lasting rules.

items.headline: Vistra Form 8-K filed Nov 5 (items 2.01, 2.03, 3.02, 7.01, 9.01) and a Schedule 13G/A (holder filing) on EDGAR
items.why: Item 2.01 is the completion of the Cogentrix purchase, which Vistra announced by press release on Oct 30 (before the window) and which the research already counts in full (cost, about 5.0M shares, assumed debt). I could not open the 8-K text (www.sec.gov blocks automated fetches), so the 2.03, 3.02 and 7.01 contents are unverified (fetch budget / site block) and I did not judge them; the filing list itself is verified from the EDGAR JSON.

items.headline: VST price: close 120.29 on Nov 4 (down 13.8% from 139.59), 112.89 on Nov 5 (down about 6.2%) on volume of 20.4M and 15.3M shares
items.why: Price data only (Twelve Data daily bars); the Nov 5 bar may be partial. The Nov 5 fall is larger than the 4-5% in the brief. A price move is not a thesis trigger; the 115 level is the supervisor's reference for when the thesis would be failing, and what breaks it is the market pricing a lasting Texas block or a weak 2027 guide, which the Nov 6 call tests.

items.headline: KeyBanc downgrade of Vistra (as reported in the brief)
items.why: Three searches found no dated KeyBanc downgrade story for Nov 4-5 (results were older KeyBanc initiation and unrelated items; the linked itiger page is undated in the snippet and was not opened), so the downgrade and its stated reasons are unverified. Even if real, an analyst rating change on the Texas risk is minor under the rules.
